topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and frames how it builds on previously introduced immunological concepts.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental principles by which the innate immune system recognizes pathogens and cellular damage through conserved molecular patterns and compartmentalized receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Pathways and the Inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major families of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling mechanisms, and the assembly of downstream inflammatory complexes such as the inflammasome.

topics.label: Acute Inflammatory Cascade and Immune Cell Trafficking
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell trafficking and fluid dynamics, as well as the severe pathological risks that arise when inflammatory activation becomes systemic.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the processes that terminate inflammatory signaling and determine whether tissue returns to homeostasis or develops chronic inflammatory pathology.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture and previews the next lecture on the complement system.
